answer: Each identity must deliver one batch of basalt aggregate and lock a 70-credit bond. A lab sieves the batch and records its shale fines share on a ticket binding weight, sieve curve, and identity key. An auditor recomputes the curve from the sample weights; a mismatch or reused ticket burns the bond. The first test costs 30, the kth costs 30+5(k-1), the 1000th costs 5025, so 1000 fakes pay 2,527,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-batch ring fails because one batch yields one cipher ticket; reuse keeps the same weight and curve. An honest trader pays 30 once and gets the bond back.
